chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr and Fadala from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a mukatab (a slave who has contracted to pay a sum for his freedom) who pays part of his manumission contract, then dies, leaving a son from his own concubine. He said: 'If it was stipulated that if he became unable to pay, he would return to slavery, then his son returns as a slave along with the concubine. And if it was not stipulated, his son becomes free, and he returns the remainder of the manumission sum to the master, and his son inherits whatever remains.'

key_terms.بَقِيَّةَ الْمُكَاتَبَةِ: The remaining balance of the manumission fee.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum in installments in exchange for his freedom.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The manumission contract or the agreed-upon sum for freedom.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the son of a slave who dies after paying part of his manumission contract?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance and status dynamics for a mukatab’s son upon the father's death, distinguishing between conditional and unconditional manumission contracts. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that unless explicitly stipulated, the son inherits freedom and the remaining debt, reflecting the merciful interpretation of slavery laws in Shia fiqh. The ruling underscores the importance of contractual stipulations (*shurut*) in determining the transition from slavery to freedom and subsequent inheritance rights.
